logline: A struggling comedian's act of kindness to a down-and-out woman at a bar ignites a stalking campaign that exposes the shame he's been carrying since long before she found him.

renewal.note: A limited series, seven episodes, complete as aired. Richard Gadd has not indicated plans for continuation.

bollymeter.basis: 98% on Rotten Tomatoes; critics called it one of the most formally and emotionally honest pieces of autofiction the medium had produced - Richard Gadd wrote, performed, and exposed himself to an extent that made most confession-based drama look cautious.

pull_quotes.text: Baby Reindeer is devastating, unflinching autofiction - Richard Gadd announces himself as one of the most singular voices in television.

seasons.review_body: Baby Reindeer arrived as one of 2024's most discussed television events. Based on Richard Gadd's stage play and his own experience of stalking and sexual abuse, the seven episodes tracked a man undone by both the stalker he'd attracted and the crime committed against him that he'd never processed. The structural intelligence was in making both stories simultaneous - the stalking both a narrative and a mirror. Critics at 98% used language about courage and necessity that they rarely deploy. The audience score of 7.9 on IMDb reflected a show that was admired more than it was easily consumed. The BAFTA and Emmy wins that followed placed it among the decade's landmark limited series.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A bartender hands a weeping stranger a free cup of tea - and sets off a seven-episode spiral he cannot control. The premiere builds dread from the mundane, grounding the obsessive spiral in Donny's own generosity and guilt rather than Martha's threat. Gadd's dual role as writer and lead gives the hour an autobiographical intimacy that distinguishes it from conventional stalker narratives.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The free cup of tea - a small act of charity that the entire series reveals as the hinge point of everything that follows.
episode_reviews.review_body: Baby Reindeer's opening episode does something quietly devastating: it locates its horror not in threat but in generosity. Donny Dunn, a flailing comedian working a London pub, gives a cup of tea to a weeping stranger named Martha. Creator and star Richard Gadd uses this act of ordinary kindness as the load-bearing beam of everything that follows. Critics praised the episode for refusing to cast Martha as a monster from the outset, instead building dread from Donny's own complicity in the contact that grows. The Guardian noted Gadd's performance as raw and precisely calibrated - self-deprecating in a way that implicates rather than excuses. At 98% on Rotten Tomatoes, the premiere is the entry point critics agreed delivered on every promise the title's strange specificity made.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 4
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Episode 4 is where Baby Reindeer announces its full ambition. As the stalking by Martha escalates in the present, a sustained flashback surfaces the assault that shaped Donny's silences and compromises. This is not a thriller episode - it is an anatomy of how victims internalise shame, and the most formally brave hour of the series.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The flashback to Donny's time with Darrien - the scene that retroactively reconfigures the first three episodes and the nature of what viewers have been watching.
episode_reviews.review_body: Episode 4 is the pivot around which Baby Reindeer's full moral complexity reveals itself. As the stalking by Martha escalates into thousands of messages, the episode introduces the TV writer Darrien through extended flashback, surfacing the assault that shaped Donny's silences and compromises. Critics identified this as the hour where Gadd's project announced its real ambition: not a procedural about a stalker but an excavation of how victims internalise shame. Variety praised the episode for the formal bravery of staging the most difficult material not as melodrama but as the texture of a working friendship curdled by power. The 98% Rotten Tomatoes critical consensus cited this episode as the proof that Baby Reindeer was doing something more serious than a thriller.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 7
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Baby Reindeer ends not with closure but with honest complication. The legal proceedings reach their conclusion, the stand-up set gets its airing, and Gadd's final scene is the series' most genuinely unsettling - for reasons that only resolve in the last minutes. A finale that earns its discomfort.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Donny watching Martha on CCTV one final time - the ambivalence of that expression is what the entire series was building toward.
episode_reviews.review_body: The finale of Baby Reindeer does not provide conventional catharsis. Martha receives a sentence. Donny records a stand-up set he has been building across all seven episodes. But Gadd saves his most uncomfortable move for last: a closing scene that implicates rather than resolves. Critics praised the finale's refusal to let Donny off the hook even after legal resolution - asking what it costs a person to tell their own story. IndieWire named it one of the best finales of 2024, precisely because it denied the audience the comfort it had been carefully set up to want. The series won six Emmy Awards including Outstanding Limited Series, with the finale cited as the culmination of Gadd's formal and emotional ambition.
